title: It’s all about robustness — Tile 2 (UNIT16 hole grid)
source: Tile 1 use-case list, reworded for the hole plate, plus Tile 2 items (3.4, 4.6, 5.4, 6.4, section 8)

cases.title: Worn or scratched plate — part of a bar is thinner or rubbed
Foreign tape or debris crossing the grid diagonally — gets mistaken for a real bar
Dirty or dusty plate — less contrast between bars and holes
Plate seam or joint — a thin dark gap splits one bar into two pieces
Uneven lighting across the frame — one side dimmer than the other
Glare or bright spot on the plate
Shadow across the grid — from the robot, a person, or an object
Too dark — weak contrast
Too bright — washed out, contrast lost
Camera not pointed straight down — slightly tilted mount
Camera height changes — changes how big things look, throws off distance
Bar spacing not exactly what the code expects — plate made a bit off size
Lens bend — bars far from the image centre look curved
Turning too fast — angle jumps too much between frames to follow
Moving very slowly between junctions — looks stopped when it isn't
Motion blur — image smears when moving fast
Turn stopped before it finished
Sudden bump, drop, or collision
Fast back-and-forth over a junction — position must not jump to the wrong junction
Two junctions in view at the same time
Junction cut off at the edge of the frame
Junction missing or broken
Camera half way between two code junctions — only the plain wide bar is near (must not be used for X)
Robot's path not centred on the frame
Loose tape or debris crossing the grid
Small objects sitting on the grid — dust, dropped parts
Cables or wires crossing the floor
Pod legs in the big round holes
Wrong mm-per-pixel setting — distances read wrong
Wrong lens setting (K1) — lines stay bent or get over-corrected
Settings drift over time — from heat or age
Code hole filled wrong on the prototype — one bit flipped
Code block partly out of the frame
Code read while moving fast or turning
Plain junction pattern that looks like a code
